The dose described in this report is very high, potentially beyond Erowid's 'heavy' range, and could pose serious health risks or result in unwanted, extreme effects. Sometimes extremely high doses reported are errors rather than actual doses used.]
Hyperglycaemic blood glucose levels seem to increase the effects of the anticholinergic.  Most notably delirium, decreased coordination, reduced vision clarity, erectile disfunction, and muscle spasms. High doses can result in convulsions lasting 10-20 minutes. Loss of coordination.
